question: What is the main job of an Automated External Defibrillator (AED) during a cardiac arrest?

options.A: Provide mechanical chest compressions at a steady rate
options.B: Pump oxygen directly into the lungs of the patient
options.C: Measure the exact blood pressure of an unresponsive person
options.D: Deliver an electrical shock to reset an abnormal heart rhythm

explanation: Think of an AED as a smart device that checks the heart rhythm and gives a quick shock only when needed to get the heart beating right again. You've got this! [learn more](GNS212_U2_T2#GNS212_U2_T2_h1)

question: Why is using an AED as quickly as possible so important during cardiac arrest?

options.A: It automatically contacts the local police department for help
options.B: It permanently cures any underlying heart disease causing the arrest
options.C: It replaces the need to ever perform chest compressions
options.D: Survival rates drop significantly with every minute that defibrillation is delayed

explanation: Every single minute counts! Without blood flow, the brain quickly loses oxygen, so acting fast truly saves lives. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T2#GNS212_U2_T2_h1)

question: Which patient sign means you should grab and attach an AED right away?

options.A: Severe chest pain and heavy sweating
options.B: Confusion and mild shortness of breath
options.C: High fever and a rapid pulse rate

explanation: An AED is meant for sudden cardiac arrest. We look for someone who has collapsed, doesn't respond, and isn't breathing normally. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T2#GNS212_U2_T2_h2)

question: What happens if an AED is accidentally used on someone whose heart is beating normally?

options.A: The heart will instantly stop due to the excess electrical current
options.B: The device will analyze the rhythm and refuse to deliver a shock
options.C: The machine will automatically start delivering CPR compressions
options.D: The internal battery of the device will permanently burn out

explanation: Don't worry, AEDs are very smart! They scan the heart first and will block any shock if the heart rhythm is normal. They won't harm a healthy beat. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T2#GNS212_U2_T2_h2)

question: What is the job of the sticky adhesive pads that come with an AED?

options.A: Secure the patient firmly to the flat floor surface
options.B: Deliver a continuous supply of medical oxygen to the lungs
options.C: Transmit electrical current from the machine to the patient's heart
options.D: Measure the exact body temperature of the victim

explanation: The pads act as the bridge. They stick to the skin to read the heart rhythm and deliver the life-saving shock safely. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T2#GNS212_U2_T2_h3)

question: Why should you regularly check the status indicator light on an AED machine?

options.A: To calibrate the internal thermometer for accurate skin readings
options.B: To measure how many shocks are left in the main computer processor
options.C: To ensure the voice volume is loud enough for a noisy room
options.D: To confirm that the internal battery and system components are operational

explanation: Routine checks make sure the machine is ready to work the exact second an emergency happens. Good nursing practice! [learn more](GNS212_U2_T2#GNS212_U2_T2_h3)

question: Where should you place the two AED pads on an adult patient's bare chest?

options.A: Center of the chest and middle of the back
options.B: Left side of the ribs and right side of the abdomen
options.C: Both shoulders near the neck collarbones
options.D: Upper right chest and lower left ribcage

explanation: Placing one pad on the upper right and the other on the lower left lets the electrical current flow diagonally right through the heart muscle. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T2#GNS212_U2_T2_h4)

question: What is the very next thing you must do after the AED delivers a shock?

options.A: Check the carotid pulse for at least one full minute
options.B: Turn the machine off and wait for the ambulance crew
options.C: Remove the sticky pads and wipe the skin with alcohol
options.D: Resume chest compressions and CPR for two minutes

explanation: Right after a shock, don't wait—jump right back into CPR starting with chest compressions to keep blood moving! [learn more](GNS212_U2_T2#GNS212_U2_T2_h4)

question: How should you handle an implanted pacemaker lump when placing an AED pad?

options.A: Refuse to use the AED because pacemakers block all shocks
options.B: Place the pad at least one inch away from the device lump
options.C: Place the pad directly over the lump to boost the shock
options.D: Cut out the pacemaker wires before attaching the sticky pads

explanation: Keep the pad about an inch away from a pacemaker lump so the machine's energy goes into the heart instead of damaging the device. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T2#GNS212_U2_T2_h5)

question: What safety step is required if a patient experiencing cardiac arrest is lying in a puddle of water?

options.A: Turn off all nearby electrical appliances in the room
options.B: Double the number of chest compressions you deliver
options.C: Move the patient to a dry area and dry the chest
options.D: Place rubber mats under your own shoes while working

explanation: Water conducts electricity. Moving the patient to dry ground and wiping their chest ensures the shock goes through the heart, not out into the water. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T2#GNS212_U2_T2_h5)

question: What usually causes an AED to flash a 'Check Pads' error message?

options.A: The patient's heart rate is too fast for the machine to read
options.B: The rescuer is pressing the shock button at the wrong time
options.C: Loose cable connections or moisture on the patient's skin
options.D: The battery inside the computer unit is completely dead

explanation: If pads aren't sticking well or the skin is wet, the machine can't get a good connection. A quick dry and press usually fixes it! [learn more](GNS212_U2_T2#GNS212_U2_T2_h6)

question: What must you do immediately when the AED announces 'Movement Detected'?

options.A: Shake the patient harder to restart the heart rhythm
options.B: Unplug the machine and replace both electrode pads
options.C: Stop chest compressions and ensure everyone steps back
options.D: Increase the speed of rescue breaths being delivered

explanation: Movement—even from CPR—can trick the AED into reading the wrong thing. Always step back and stay clear while it analyzes. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T2#GNS212_U2_T2_h6)

question: What should you do with the AED pads if the patient suddenly wakes up and starts breathing?

options.A: Move both pads to the patient's back to keep the skin warm
options.B: Peel them off immediately and throw them in the trash
options.C: Leave the pads attached to the chest in case arrest recurs
options.D: Wipe them down with bleach and pack them in the box

explanation: Leave the pads on! A recovered patient can still slip back into cardiac arrest very quickly, and you want the AED ready to go. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T2#GNS212_U2_T2_h7)

question: Why is placing an unconscious, breathing patient into the recovery position so important?

options.A: It keeps the airway clear and prevents aspiration of fluids
options.B: It stops involuntary muscle spasms in the arms and legs
options.C: It makes it easier to reapply the AED pads if needed
options.D: It lowers the patient's elevated blood pressure quickly

explanation: The recovery position uses gravity to keep the tongue and saliva from blocking the airway of someone who is knocked out. Safety first! [learn more](GNS212_U2_T2#GNS212_U2_T2_h7)
